ART DIRECTION: BERTH SCHEDULE. Cool mist gray #EDF2F0 and pale sea-glass canvas, deep ink navy #142C38, restrained muted teal #6C9890, ONE focal signal-coral #F27759 for the open slot. Crisp grotesque sans, beautifully set large headline, monospaced tabular times and fictional IDs. Strict timetable grid with thin hairline rules, ample white space, left-aligned strong editorial hierarchy. An elegant custom abstract W logo built from two berth shapes; wordmark WaitListFit.
The hero's lower half contains an architectural horizontal clinic-day timetable of calm neutral occupied rectangles along a rail, one coral outlined open berth at 10:30–11:00. The open slot is visually dominant. No boats, anchors, nautical illustrations or literal ports. Three candidate cards approach on parallel fine tracks; A and B subdued but reasons fully readable, C neutral and outlined awaiting review. The next scroll chapter continues the same thin timetable rail down into a scheduler rationale panel. Tiny elegant visual arrows and sequential positions suggest the intended motion: cancellation block drops away, gap gently pulses, three candidates arrive, rejected candidates dim, and C docks only on Simulate approval. Depict the review-before-docking frame, with a dotted path, not a completed fill. Use flat graphic precision, only very gentle shadows, zero glassmorphism, no gradients, no oversized pills. This is the user's preferred territory: exceptionally refined, original operational timetable design, luxurious whitespace, coherent continuous background.

ART DIRECTION: CONSTRAINT MAP. Precision architectural blueprint on warm paper white #F7F5EF, fine slate-blue #607589 construction lines, deep slate #273D50 text and a restrained amber #D99A33 highlight. Very different composition from a timetable hero: large editorial headline in a compact left column occupying 42%; hero right and across lower page is a generous intricate but legible constraint-map drawing. Crisp neo-grotesque headings, monospaced annotation labels, tiny numbered coordinate marks, subtle paper texture and technical drafting hierarchy. Logo a simple intersecting open-square W geometry and WaitListFit wordmark. No nautical elements, no physical calendar, no dark dashboard, no floating generic feature cards. Background construction lines continue naturally between sections.
Make the product metaphor dominant: exactly seven clearly labeled horizontal operational lanes: Clinician, Room, Visit length, Equipment, Authorization, Interpreter, Transport. Their thin paths connect a 10:30–11:00 / 30 MIN open-slot outline to three labeled CAND-A, CAND-B, CAND-C endpoints. Amber indicates the selected Room and Interpreter constraint toggles. A path ends at visible 'Room mismatch'; B path ends at 'Interpreter unavailable'; C stays slate-blue, labeled 'Pending scheduler review', not automatically booked. Constraints are toggle controls visible on a narrow left map edge. Active constraints remove candidates from consideration but leave faint outlines and exclusion reasons in the drawing. Clear amber brackets emphasize exceptions; no clinical judgments. Every demo labeled DEMO — SYNTHETIC DATA.
Lower chapter 'One cancellation. Three candidates.' shows an enlarged extracted candidate rationale on the same paper plane, ruled source/evidence annotation table, source 'Synthetic constraint version v03', fictional owner 'Scheduler role S-01', timestamp '13 Oct 2026 · 10:15'. A square-corner dark slate 'Simulate approval' button with 'No appointment booked' adjacent. Motion implied through alternating fine lane overlays and one highlighted connected path. Premium technical editorial website, generous breathing room, exact lines, warm enough to feel human but decisively blueprint-oriented.

ART DIRECTION: DEPARTURE BOARD. An unforgettable precision split-flap display as the sole expressive hero artifact, on an otherwise bright refined ivory #F4F2EB and charcoal #252925 editorial SaaS page. Muted signal amber #D9AF5D and a small sage indication, normal typography everywhere else. Elegant modern grotesque headline, not monospace headlines, no serif. A clean compact WaitListFit wordmark with a tiny logo made of two offset split-flap rectangles. Wide thin navigation, huge generous margin, subtle horizontal rules. Hero headline in balanced centered lines above the display, CTAs below headline, with a spacious instrumental feeling. Different arrangement from prior directions: center-aligned opening, broad dark board anchored beneath.
The physical dark split-flap board has authentic tiny hinge lines, restrained tactile material, sharp cream letterforms and horizontal seam. Limit letter cells to a single prominent status strip reading 'PENDING APPROVAL' and compact '10:30' time display. Surrounding board information uses readable ordinary type, not a wall of letter tiles. Board label 'TUESDAY 13 OCTOBER 2026'; '30 MIN · ROOM R-02 · D-01'. Persistent DEMO — SYNTHETIC DATA above board. State progression on a narrow normal-font legend underneath: OPEN → PENDING APPROVAL → FILLED · SIMULATED. Current pending status highlighted. Adjacent footnote 'Final state appears only after Simulate approval. No appointment booked.' Show one or two subtly mid-flip time tiles only to evoke motion, keep status readable. No airline logos, airplanes, airport photography, flight routes or transportation language. This is specialty clinic scheduling.
Below hero the continuous ivory page opens into 'One cancellation. Three candidates.' with a calm editorial three-row review list: CAND-A / Room mismatch; CAND-B / Interpreter unavailable at 10:30; CAND-C / Pending scheduler review. A slim evidence bar shows Room R-02, 30 min, EQ-01, authorization, interpreter, transport. Lower demo includes source v03, reviewer S-01, 'Simulate approval'. Make the artifact premium and memorable without extending split-flap typography into navigation, text or lower demo. Tight craft, restrained palette, substantial whitespace, no generic floating cards and no spurious metrics.
